top_choice_rationale: P001 rewards a distinct, mature and independently reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms removes Doppler, recoil and first-order light-shift errors, a different step from the comb and single-ion prizes, and the 10^-18 level has been reproduced at JILA, RIKEN, NIST, PTB and SYRTE. The two-name allocation (Katori for the concept, Ye for the record-accuracy demonstration and clock-comparison physics) has the smallest gap between credited names and the discovery of any option; the citation should be worded around the lattice clock to avoid reading as a second comb prize. P002 is a genuine and important discovery but is less mature on the pairing mechanism and has attribution problems (Cao and others outside the three names), so I rank it second, above no award.
recusal_note: Profile-based conflict: long-running scientific collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and papers with the Lund attosecond group, ETH Zurich (Keller) collaborations, and atomic-physics theory work in the same community as the optical-clock candidates; no documented direct collaboration with Katori or Ye, but I am not a neutral judge of the atomic-physics candidates.
